summary.automatic_F_trigger: Red team confirmed breaches of critical objectives: RED-001 (auth absence), RED-002 (state machine bypass)

findings.title: Complete Authentication Absence — Every API Endpoint Open to Anonymous Callers
findings.description: Zero authentication or authorization middleware exists anywhere in the application. All workflow state transition endpoints — including approve, reject, dispatch, hard-delete — are reachable by any unauthenticated HTTP caller. The red team confirmed this live: BUG-0001 was created, triaged, resolved, and hard-deleted; FR-0001 was created and approved — all without any credential.
findings.remediation: Add mandatory authentication middleware (JWT or API-key) before all route mounts in both Source/Backend/src/app.ts and portal/Backend/src/index.ts. Define a role model (viewer, operator, admin). Scope state-mutation endpoints to authenticated roles.

findings.title: State Machine Bypass — Items Approved with Zero Votes, No Assessment Pod
findings.description: Two independent confirmed bypass paths: (1) PATCH /api/feature-requests/:id allows direct status transitions to 'approved' with votes:[] and human_approval_approved_at:null — bypassing the vote majority check that only exists in the dedicated /approve endpoint. (2) POST /api/feature-requests/:id/deny transitions an item from 'potential' to 'denied' without any AI voting round. The entire assessment pod is skipped. FR-0002 was confirmed approved with zero votes; FR-0011 was confirmed denied with zero votes.
findings.remediation: Remove 'approved' from the PATCH-accessible status transition map. Approval/denial must only be reachable through dedicated endpoints (/approve, /force-approve, /deny) that enforce vote majority checks and require authentication with an approver role.

findings.title: IDOR — Arbitrary Cross-User Content Modification and Hard Deletion
findings.description: All endpoints use req.params.id (UUID) directly with no ownership or tenancy check. Any anonymous caller who knows a work item ID can read, overwrite, or permanently delete it. Confirmed live: FR-0003 content overwritten by a second anonymous session; BUG-0001 permanently hard-deleted with no recoverability.
findings.remediation: Implement ownership checks on all :id routes. After authentication is added, verify the requesting user's identity against resource ownership. Require an explicit admin role for hard-delete operations.

findings.title: Bug Lifecycle State Machine Fully Traversable Without Authentication
findings.description: An anonymous caller walked BUG-0001 through its full lifecycle: reported → triaged → in_development → resolved with no authentication, no engineer assignment, no review gate. The PATCH handler allows arbitrary status transitions without any guard. Confirmed live.
findings.remediation: Require authentication AND a role check (engineer or admin) for triage, resolve, close, and reopen endpoints. PATCH must not allow status transitions to resolved states without role enforcement.

findings.title: Pagination Bypass — Full Dataset Exfiltrated in a Single Unauthenticated Request
findings.description: The limit query parameter is accepted but not enforced server-side. GET /api/feature-requests?limit=1 returned ALL 10 items; GET /api/search?q= (empty query) returned ALL 14 items in a single unauthenticated response including IDs, titles, descriptions, statuses, vote decisions, and dependency graphs. The limit parameter was silently ignored.
findings.remediation: Enforce a server-side MAX_LIMIT cap (e.g., 100). Return HTTP 400 for out-of-range values. Require minimum 2 characters for the search q parameter. Apply the same cap to /api/dashboard/activity.

findings.title: Stored XSS — Malicious Script Payloads Persisted Verbatim
findings.description: POST /api/feature-requests accepted and persisted in title and in description verbatim. Confirmed: GET /api/feature-requests/FR-0010 returns the payload unmodified. Any frontend rendering these fields as innerHTML would execute arbitrary JavaScript.
findings.remediation: Sanitize all text inputs server-side using an allowlist (strip HTML/script tags using DOMPurify or equivalent). Never use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user content. Add a Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Orchestrator Proxy — SSRF Attack Vector
findings.status: Theoretical (Attempted — orchestrator offline in test env)
findings.description: POST /api/orchestrator/* blindly proxies to ORCHESTRATOR_URL env var with no authentication check. Confirmed: the request was forwarded to localhost:8080 (received a 502 because the orchestrator was offline in the test environment). In production with orchestrator reachable, this allows any anonymous caller to trigger agent team runs, exfiltrate pipeline data, or submit malicious pipeline tasks. ORCHESTRATOR_URL is not validated against an allowlist, so injecting a different value would achieve full SSRF.
findings.remediation: Add authentication middleware on /api/orchestrator route. Validate ORCHESTRATOR_URL against a trusted allowlist. Log all proxy invocations with caller identity.

findings.title: Cascade Auto-Dispatch Fires on Blocker Rejection — Business Logic Flaw
findings.description: DISPATCH_TRIGGER_STATUSES includes Rejected. When a blocker item is rejected, onItemResolved fires and auto-dispatches any approved dependent items — even though the blocker's work was never completed. An attacker can create a high-priority blocked item, immediately reject its blocker, and force the dependent item into in-progress without the blocking concern ever being addressed.
findings.remediation: Remove Rejected from DISPATCH_TRIGGER_STATUSES. Cascade auto-dispatch should only fire on Completed status. A rejected blocker means the blocking concern is unresolved. Alternatively, add a human review step before cascade dispatch fires.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Webhook Intake — No HMAC Signature Validation, No Enum Guards
findings.owasp: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.description: Both /api/intake/zendesk and /api/intake/automated accept payloads with no authentication and no HMAC-SHA256 signature verification. Additionally, type and priority fields are not validated against their enum types unlike the main POST /api/work-items route. Any caller can forge Zendesk events and inject arbitrary enum values into the store.
findings.remediation: Validate incoming webhook payloads using HMAC-SHA256 against a shared secret in an env variable. Reject requests with missing or invalid signatures. Add the same enum guard used in workItems.ts to both intake routes.

findings.title: Docker Socket Mounted in Orchestrator Container — Container Escape Vector
findings.description: The orchestrator container is granted access to the host Docker daemon socket (/var/run/docker.sock). A compromised orchestrator container can spawn privileged containers, mount host filesystems, and achieve full host OS compromise. Platform scope — remediation requires a solo session.
findings.remediation: Assess whether the orchestrator actually needs direct Docker API access. If so, use a Docker socket proxy (e.g., docker-socket-proxy) that limits the available API surface. Consider Docker-in-Docker if isolation is required.
findings.scope_note: Platform scope — requires solo session per project rules

findings.title: No Transport Layer Security — All Traffic in Plaintext
findings.description: The backend binds to plain HTTP. No TLS configuration exists anywhere in source. All API traffic — including any future credentials and tokens — is transmitted in the clear.
findings.remediation: Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy (nginx/Caddy/AWS ALB) with a valid certificate. Enforce HSTS. Add redirect-to-HTTPS middleware in Express.

findings.title: No CORS Policy — Cross-Origin Requests Unrestricted
findings.description: No CORS middleware applied. Combined with complete absence of authentication, cross-origin request forgery is trivially possible from any origin.
findings.remediation: Install cors and configure explicit allowlist: app.use(cors({ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true })). Block all other origins.

findings.title: Required Audit Events Not Emitted — SOC2 CC7.1 Violation
findings.description: Four mandatory audit event types (login_attempt, permission_denied, state_transition, data_export) are not emitted as structured audit log events anywhere in the codebase. changeHistory captures domain records but is not an audit log — no actor identity, no integrity protection, not queryable as events.
findings.remediation: Implement a dedicated audit-log service emitting structured JSON events with event_type, actor_id, resource_type, resource_id, timestamp, outcome. Emit state_transition events in the workflow service. Emit login_attempt and permission_denied events once auth is added.

findings.title: No Session Management, Token Expiry, or MFA
findings.description: No session layer exists. No session tokens are issued, no token expiry is enforced, no MFA is available. OWASP-ASVS L2 specifically requires session binding, idle/absolute timeout, and MFA support.
findings.remediation: After authentication is added (MERGED-001), implement stateless JWT with short expiry (15 min access / 8 hr refresh) or server-side sessions with idle timeout ≤30 min. Add TOTP-based MFA for administrative roles.

findings.title: No Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) — No Principle of Least Privilege
findings.description: No user roles or permission scopes. No concept of operator vs admin. All endpoints are equally open. The principle of least privilege is entirely absent.
findings.remediation: Define role model (viewer, operator, admin). Implement RBAC middleware that checks authenticated user's role before mutation endpoints. Dispatch and approve must require elevated privileges.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics Endpoint — 39 Metric Families Exposed
findings.description: GET /metrics is publicly accessible with no auth. Red team confirmed: 39 metric families exposed including feature_request_status_transitions_total, bug_status_transitions_total, and http_request_duration_ms (full route map visible). An attacker can map all API routes, understand approval/denial rates, and plan targeted attacks.
findings.remediation: Restrict /metrics to internal network via reverse-proxy allow/deny rules, or add a bearer-token check (METRICS_TOKEN env var). Never expose on a public-facing port.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers — No helmet, CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options
findings.description: Express sets no HTTP security headers. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options. No explicit CORS policy. X-Powered-By: Express header reveals the server stack.
findings.remediation: Add app.use(helmet()) as first middleware. Configure contentSecurityPolicy, hsts (production), disable x-powered-by. Add cors middleware with explicit origin allowlist.

findings.title: Host Claude Credentials File Bind-Mounted into Orchestrator Container
findings.description: The operator's local Claude API credentials file is bind-mounted read-only into the orchestrator container. A compromised orchestrator can read and exfiltrate these credentials. Platform scope — requires solo session.
findings.remediation: Pass credential value as environment variable or Docker secret rather than mounting the raw file: environment: CLAUDE_API_KEY=${CLAUDE_API_KEY}
findings.scope_note: Platform scope — requires solo session per project rules

findings.title: No Rate Limiting — Memory Exhaustion DoS via Intake Spam
findings.description: No rate-limiting middleware on any endpoint. Combined with unauthenticated intake endpoints, an attacker can issue unlimited POST requests flooding the in-memory store and exhausting Node.js heap. Limit parameter has no server-enforced maximum.
findings.remediation: Install express-rate-limit with a global limiter. Apply stricter limits to mutation endpoints. Cap the limit query parameter to a configurable maximum (100).

findings.title: Soft-Deleted Blocker Permanently Blocks Dependent Item Dispatch
findings.description: findById returns undefined for soft-deleted items. computeHasUnresolvedBlockers treats undefined blocker as still blocking (!blocker evaluates to true). A dependent item can never be dispatched after its blocker is soft-deleted, even though the blocker was explicitly removed from the system.
findings.remediation: In computeHasUnresolvedBlockers, treat a deleted blocker as resolved (remove the dependency link on deletion, or check deleted state explicitly). Alternatively, when soft-deleting a blocker, automatically remove all blockedBy references to it.

findings.title: No Data Retention or Hard-Deletion Policy
findings.description: softDelete sets deleted:true but records remain in-memory indefinitely and are recoverable via direct ID lookup. No hard-delete mechanism, no retention schedule. All data lost on restart — data integrity risk.
findings.remediation: Implement a persistent store (database). Add hard-delete function. Define retention policy (completed/rejected items purged after N days) and implement scheduled purge job.

findings.title: Unvalidated overrideRoute Enum Value Stored As-Is
findings.description: The overrideRoute field from POST /api/work-items/:id/route is passed through TypeScript type assertions but never validated at runtime. An attacker can send arbitrary strings that get persisted in the route field.
findings.remediation: Add runtime enum validation: if (body?.overrideRoute && !Object.values(WorkItemRoute).includes(body.overrideRoute)) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Invalid overrideRoute value' });

findings.title: Internal Error Messages Echoed to HTTP Clients
findings.description: Caught error messages from internal services are returned verbatim in HTTP 500 responses in workflow route handlers, leaking internal IDs and system state. The global errorHandler correctly returns generic messages, but per-route try/catch blocks bypass it.
findings.remediation: For unexpected errors, return a generic message to the client and log detail server-side only. Reserve specific messages for domain errors (400/404).

findings.title: Missing /api/search Route — Referenced by Frontend, Not Implemented
findings.description: The frontend API client calls GET /api/search?q=<query> but this route is not registered in app.ts. Returns 404. Forward-looking XSS/injection risk if implemented without input validation.
findings.remediation: Implement /api/search with proper input validation and sanitization. Require minimum query length. Add the route to the backend router.

findings.title: Pagination NaN/Negative Integer Parameters Silently Fail
findings.description: Invalid limit/page values (0, -1, NaN, non-numeric) produce silent incorrect behavior: totalPages: Infinity when limit=0, empty data arrays when page=0 or page=-1, no error response. Frontend may enter an infinite pagination loop.
findings.remediation: Add input validation for limit and page: enforce positive integers within range, return HTTP 400 for invalid values. Cap limit to MAX_LIMIT.

red_team_summary.scope_note: Pen-tester analyzed Source/Backend/ (work-items API); running container is portal/Backend/. All vulnerability classes confirmed valid — architectural patterns identical.
